canonical_production_data_mutation_note: Real, intentional, additive-only mutations: (1) one idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS migration; (2) a real run of scripts/phase78-cluster-errors.mts (user-approved) populated 1 real row in error_clusters and set cluster_id on all 148 previously-null error_events rows. No row was overwritten or deleted; all mutation was populating previously-empty/-null state. Zero writes to error_suggestions, source files, Qdrant, Valkey, or Neo4j at any point.
reason: The reader/writer schema disconnect (the deepest bug) is fixed and verified live end to end. Blocked now on a legitimate data-quality edge case -- this run's only real cluster has no source-mappable file path -- not a code bug. generateProposal()/Ornith itself was still not reached.
narrative: Investigating why PHASE78-LIVE-PROPOSAL-NO-PERSIST-01 could not find an eligible cluster led through a chain of 8 real, independently-confirmed bugs across two scripts and one schema file, all fixed and verified live this session.

bugsFoundInOrder.fix: Applied drizzle/manual/20260413_route_health_tables.sql (idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS).

bugsFoundInOrder.bug: NOT EXISTS subquery compared error_suggestions.cluster_id (uuid) to error_cluster.cluster_id (varchar) -- 'operator does not exist: uuid = character varying'.
bugsFoundInOrder.fix: Superseded entirely by bug #8's rewrite (query no longer reads from error_cluster at all).

bugsFoundInOrder.bug: Imported errorClustersTable/errorEventsTable from 'src/lib/server/db/schema/index.js', which does not export them. Real definitions live in a separate directory tree: 'src/lib/db/schema/cutlass.ts'.
Imported a nonexistent function 'generateCachedEmbedding' from ollama-config.ts (only 'generateEmbedding(text)' exists).
bugsFoundInOrder.fix: Aliased import to generateEmbeddingRaw, called with single text argument.

bugsFoundInOrder.bug: errorClustersTable/errorEventsTable Drizzle declarations were stale relative to the live tables (confirmed via information_schema.columns and pg_enum): wrong column names (file_path/stack_trace vs real file/stack), missing columns (collected_at, line_number, column_number, kind, severity, pattern, error_count, route_paths, radius, last_updated), and no pgEnum types for error_kind/error_severity.
bugsFoundInOrder.fix: Rewrote both table definitions in cutlass.ts to match live columns/types exactly, using pgEnum for error_kind ('runtime'|'api'|'other') and error_severity ('info'|'warn'|'error'|'critical'). No ALTER/migration was needed -- the live database was already correct; only the TypeScript declaration was wrong.

bugsFoundInOrder.bug: The clustering insert/update block used field names (errorPattern, memberCount, lastSeenAt, updatedAt) matching neither the old nor corrected schema, and called inferClusterKind()/normalizeSeverity() to invent a taxonomy (typing/nullability/import/svelte-rune/... and info/warn/error/FATAL) that does not match the real error_kind/error_severity enums ('fatal' is not a valid severity).
bugsFoundInOrder.fix: Use the real, already-correct kind/severity values straight off the representative error_events row (ingestion already tags them correctly) instead of re-deriving a fictional taxonomy. inferClusterKind()/normalizeSeverity() left in the file, unused, rather than deleted (separate decision).

bugsFoundInOrder.bug: clusterIdStr was a fabricated string (cluster-${clusterId}) inserted into a uuid column -- would fail at the DB level with 'invalid input syntax for type uuid'.
bugsFoundInOrder.fix: Let Postgres generate the real uuid via defaultRandom(), captured via .returning({ id }), used for the per-event FK update.

bugsFoundInOrder.bug: getClustersWithoutSuggestions() read from the orphaned 'error_cluster' (singular) table, which no real writer anywhere in the repo populates, instead of the real 'error_clusters' (plural) table bug #6's fix populates.
bugsFoundInOrder.fix: Rewrote the query to read from error_clusters, LEFT JOIN LATERAL to a representative (most recently collected) error_events row for file/stack/ts_code detail. es.cluster_id = ec.id now compares uuid to uuid directly (bug #2 no longer applies -- superseded, not separately needed).

phase78ClusterErrorsRealRun.command: npx tsx scripts/phase78-cluster-errors.mts (no --dry-run, user-approved real write)
phase78ClusterErrorsRealRun.result: 148 real embeddings generated via Ollama, K-means clustered into 1 cluster (data-driven outcome, not a bug), 1 real row inserted into error_clusters (id=03ffef48-3a72-4f19-8d15-4c3afc5a494a, kind=runtime, severity=warn, error_count=148, real route_paths array), all 148 error_events rows had cluster_id set. Exit code 0.

phase78GenerateSuggestionsLiveNoPersistR.result: Correctly found the real cluster by its actual UUID (03ffef48-3a72-4f19-8d15-4c3afc5a494a) -- confirms the reader/writer disconnect (bug #8) is genuinely fixed, not just plausible. Stopped at resolveSourceSnapshot() returning null: this cluster's representative error (a Svelte onDestroy lifecycle warning) has a bundled/minified runtime stack trace with no resolvable local source file path -- a real data-quality fact about this specific error, not a code bug.

conclusion: All 8 found bugs across the full phase78-cluster-errors.mts -> error_clusters -> phase78-generate-suggestions.mts chain are fixed and verified live. This pipeline had apparently never executed successfully end to end against this database at any point before this session. generateProposal()/the real Ornith call was still not reached in this run because this run's only cluster (K-means produced exactly 1) has no source-mappable file path. Next real test (not attempted here, given session context budget): re-run against route-error data with a resolvable source file (a real TS/Svelte compile-time error rather than a bundled runtime stack trace), or tune K-means to produce more, smaller clusters so a resolvable one is more likely to surface.
RESULT_FINAL: PARTIAL_PROVEN -- 8/8 found bugs fixed and verified live end to end; the Ornith-invocation half of this gate still awaits a cluster with a resolvable source file.
